targets.title: Chord: A Scalable Peer-to-peer Lookup Service for Internet Applications
targets.authors: Ion Stoica, Robert Morris, David R. Karger, M. Frans Kaashoek, Hari Balakrishnan
targets.why_needed: Ring-topology DHT with O(log n) hops via exponentially-spaced finger table; the comparison baseline every later structured overlay (Koorde, Symphony, Viceroy, Skip+) states its own hop/state tradeoff against.

targets.title: Pastry: Scalable, Decentralized Object Location, and Routing for Large-Scale Peer-to-Peer Systems
targets.authors: Antony Rowstron, Peter Druschel
targets.why_needed: Prefix-matching routing plus a defined proximity neighbor selection procedure; needed to compare prefix routing against Kademlia's XOR routing and to source the original PNS mechanism definition.

targets.title: Tapestry: A Resilient Global-Scale Overlay for Service Deployment
targets.authors: Ben Y. Zhao, Ling Huang, Jeremy Stribling, Sean C. Rhea, Anthony D. Joseph, John Kubiatowicz
targets.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
targets.why_needed: Prefix-routing overlay with explicit fault-tolerant redundant-root replication for churn resilience; the journal version states the resilience mechanisms only sketched in the 2001 tech report.

targets.title: A Scalable Content-Addressable Network
targets.authors: Sylvia Ratnasamy, Paul Francis, Mark Handley, Richard Karp, Scott Shenker
targets.why_needed: d-dimensional coordinate-space routing, the structural opposite of ring/prefix/XOR routing; needed as the fourth routing-geometry family in the geometry-comparison analysis.

targets.title: Koorde: A Simple Degree-Optimal Distributed Hash Table
targets.authors: M. Frans Kaashoek, David R. Karger
targets.why_needed: States the routing-table-size-versus-hop-count Pareto boundary directly (2 contacts at O(log n) hops, or O(log n) contacts at O(log n / log log n) hops) via a de Bruijn graph construction; the number every 'is Kademlia's k near-optimal' claim must be checked against.

targets.title: Viceroy: A Scalable and Dynamic Emulation of the Butterfly
targets.authors: Dahlia Malkhi, Moni Naor, David Ratajczak
targets.why_needed: Constant expected degree (7) with O(log n) hops via a butterfly-network emulation, and a proof that node join/leave costs a constant number of link changes in expectation; the fixed-degree alternative to Kademlia's O(log n)-sized k-buckets.

targets.title: Symphony: Distributed Hashing in a Small World
targets.authors: Gurmeet Singh Manku, Mayank Bawa, Prabhakar Raghavan
targets.venue: USENIX Symposium on Internet Technologies and Systems
targets.why_needed: Ring topology with k long-range links per node drawn from a harmonic (Kleinberg small-world) distribution, giving O(log^2 n / k) expected hops for an explicit, adjustable per-node link budget k; the tunable-state-versus-hop-count point against Kademlia's fixed k.

targets.title: A Performance vs. Cost Framework for Evaluating DHT Design Tradeoffs Under Churn
targets.authors: Jinyang Li, Jeremy Stribling, Robert Morris, M. Frans Kaashoek, Thomer M. Gil
targets.why_needed: Introduces Accordion's self-tuning bandwidth-budget DHT (routing-table density inversely proportional to identifier distance) and the PVC (performance-vs-cost) simulation framework used to compare Chord, Kademlia, Tapestry, and other DHTs under a common churn model at a matched bandwidth budget rather than a matched table size.

targets.title: Handling Churn in a DHT
targets.authors: Sean Rhea, Dennis Geels, Timothy Roscoe, John Kubiatowicz
targets.why_needed: Introduces Bamboo; isolates three independent design choices (reactive vs. periodic recovery, TCP-style adaptive timeout, proximity neighbor selection) and measures each one's separate contribution to lookup consistency under Kazaa-derived churn rates, which is the source paper the already-read HSkip+/PNS claims trace back to.

targets.title: Efficient Routing for Peer-to-Peer Overlays
targets.authors: Anjali Gupta, Barbara Liskov, Rodrigo Rodrigues
targets.why_needed: One-hop DHT design: every node maintains a proactively-updated full routing table so any lookup completes in one hop, at O(n) per-node maintenance state and bandwidth; the opposite end of the hop-count-vs-state Pareto frontier from Koorde's 2-contact minimum.

targets.title: Democratizing Content Publication with Coral
targets.authors: Michael J. Freedman, Eric Freudenthal, David Mazieres
targets.why_needed: A structured overlay (Coral, a hierarchical DSHT) whose lookup step optimizes for round-trip-time-measured network proximity over identifier closeness and uses sloppy (rate-limited, multi-valued) hashing rather than exact key-to-node mapping; a candidate for the brief's request for a design that departs from the pure identifier-closeness routing premise.

targets.title: Kelips: Building an Efficient and Stable P2P DHT through Increased Memory and Background Overhead
targets.authors: Indranil Gupta, Kenneth P. Birman, Prakash Linga, Alan J. Demers, Robbert van Renesse
targets.why_needed: Replaces incremental identifier-closeness forwarding with O(sqrt(n))-sized affinity groups maintained by continuous background gossip, giving O(1) expected lookup hops at O(sqrt(n)) per-node state and a steady background bandwidth cost instead of an on-demand routing cost; the clearest published example of abandoning multi-hop identifier-closeness routing while keeping a structured (hash-partitioned) design.

targets.title: Secure Routing for Structured Peer-to-Peer Overlay Networks
targets.authors: Miguel Castro, Peter Druschel, Ayalvadi Ganesh, Antony Rowstron, Dan S. Wallach
targets.why_needed: Defines certified identifier assignment, redundant routing along disjoint paths, and a routing-failure test as the three-part defense against routing-table poisoning; the direct predecessor of S/Kademlia's disjoint-path defense that the already-read S/Kademlia paper's P_K success formula builds on.

targets.title: Security Considerations for Peer-to-Peer Distributed Hash Tables
targets.authors: Emil Sit, Robert Morris
targets.why_needed: First taxonomy of DHT-specific attack classes (routing-table corruption, storage denial, message-content corruption, network partition, and Sybil identity generation), stated independently of any one overlay's defense; needed as the classification scheme the later attack papers in this list are measured against.

targets.title: A Survey of DHT Security Techniques
targets.authors: Guido Urdaneta, Guillaume Pierre, Maarten van Steen
targets.why_needed: Named by the governing brief (section 4.4) as one of the densest bibliographies to mine for the DHT attack literature; needed for its own classification of Sybil, eclipse, and routing/storage defenses and for backward-mining every defense paper it cites that this list has not already captured.

targets.title: Eclipse Attacks on Overlay Networks: Threats and Defenses
targets.authors: Atul Singh, Tsuen-Wan Ngan, Peter Druschel, Dan S. Wallach
targets.why_needed: States the eclipse attack as filling a victim's entire routing table with colluding nodes so all traffic passes through the attacker, and measures a connectivity-anonymous-auditing defense against it on a real DHT deployment; the origin measurement the term 'eclipse attack' is cited to across the entire field.

targets.title: Eclipse Attacks on Bitcoin's Peer-to-Peer Network
targets.authors: Ethan Heilman, Alison Kendler, Aviv Zohar, Sharon Goldberg
targets.why_needed: Demonstrates identity-forgery-based eclipse of a deployed peer-to-peer network's connection table (not DHT routing-table poisoning, since Bitcoin's network is unstructured, but the same identity-forgery mechanism the brief asks for on routing tables) and states the countermeasures (deterministic random eviction, feeler connections) later adopted into Bitcoin Core.

targets.title: Low-Resource Eclipse Attacks on Ethereum's Peer-to-Peer Network
targets.authors: Yuval Marcus, Ethan Heilman, Sharon Goldberg
targets.why_needed: Eclipses Ethereum's Kademlia-derived node-discovery table using only a small number of attacker-controlled IP addresses, exploiting the eviction policy of the pre-discv5 Kademlia table implementation; the deployed-Kademlia identity-forgery attack the newer discv5 measurement papers (Krol, Li) state their improvement against.

targets.title: DISC-NG: Robust Service Discovery in the Ethereum Global Network
targets.authors: Michal Krol, Onur Ascigil, Sergi Rene, Alberto Sonnino, Matthieu Pigaglio, Ramin Sadre, Felix Lange, Etienne Riviere
targets.venue: IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P)
targets.why_needed: Measures discv5 (Ethereum's current Kademlia-based discovery protocol) as eclipsable at a stated rate and a plain unstructured DHT walk as eclipsable at a stated higher rate, then proposes a pseudo-random advertisement-placement mechanism deployed in devp2p that lowers it; both figures need their attacker-resource and node-count conditions extracted from the full text before being cited, not the search-snippet numbers already seen (17.8%, 59.7%).

targets.title: A Place for Everyone vs Everyone in its Place: Measuring and Attacking the Ethereum Global Network
targets.authors: Chenyu Li, Ren Zhang, Xiaorui Gong
targets.why_needed: Independent 2025 crawl-based measurement of discv5 network size and connectivity, plus a stated attack; deployed-DHT measurement squarely in the 2020-2026 window the brief asks this domain to prioritize, and a check on whether Krol et al.'s eclipse-rate figures replicate under a different measurement methodology.

targets.title: Eclipse Attacks on Ethereum's Peer-to-Peer Network
targets.authors: Ruisheng Shi, Yuxuan Liang, Zijun Guo, Qin Wang, Lina Lan, Chenfeng Wang, Zhuoyi Zheng
targets.why_needed: 2026 eclipse-attack result on the Ethereum peer-to-peer network, published after DISC-NG's proposed defense; the forward-mining catch the brief warns a superseded 2021-era result would otherwise miss — determine on retrieval whether it attacks discv5 directly, DISC-NG, or a different layer, and whether DISC-NG's defense holds against it.

targets.title: Understanding Churn in Peer-to-Peer Networks
targets.authors: Daniel Stutzbach, Reza Rejaie
targets.why_needed: Measures session-length distributions on three deployed peer-to-peer networks (not derived from any one DHT's own logs) and shows median session length is a misleading summary because the distribution is heavy-tailed; the churn-rate input every structured-overlay churn-resilience claim (Bamboo, HSkip+) needs a stated real distribution for, rather than an assumed Poisson or exponential model.

targets.title: The Impact of DHT Routing Geometry on Resilience and Proximity
targets.authors: Krishna P. Gummadi, Ramakrishna Gummadi, Steven D. Gribble, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Scott Shenker, Ion Stoica
targets.why_needed: Isolates routing geometry (tree/hypercube/ring/butterfly/XOR) as a variable independent of any single protocol and shows which geometries permit choosing among multiple next-hop candidates at each forwarding step (a prerequisite for both proximity neighbor selection and disjoint-path routing); the paper the already-read S/Kademlia paper's claim about XOR's routing flexibility ultimately traces to.

targets.title: A Global View of KAD
targets.authors: Moritz Steiner, Taoufik En-Najjary, Ernst W. Biersack
targets.why_needed: Large-scale crawl of KAD, the Kademlia-derived DHT deployed in eMule/eDonkey, giving directly measured routing-table staleness, churn, and lookup behavior on a real Kademlia deployment at a scale the original Kademlia paper's simulation did not reach; a baseline the 2020s IPFS/Ethereum Kademlia measurements can be compared against for whether deployed-Kademlia behavior changed over 15+ years.

targets.title: Exploiting KAD: Possible Uses and Misuses
targets.authors: Moritz Steiner, Taoufik En-Najjary, Ernst W. Biersack
targets.why_needed: States concrete attacks against the deployed KAD Kademlia network (routing-table poisoning, publish/retrieve denial, identity-forgery-based eclipse) executed against the live network from the same crawl infrastructure as the companion measurement paper, with the resource cost of each attack stated; a directly measured cost figure to set against Sybil/eclipse cost claims made only in simulation.

targets.title: R/Kademlia: Recursive and Topology-aware Overlay Routing
targets.authors: Bernhard Heep
targets.venue: Australasian Telecommunication Networks and Applications Conference (ATNAC)
targets.why_needed: Recursive-routing variant of Kademlia combined with proximity routing and proximity neighbor selection, stated as lower-latency under KAD-characteristic churn than iterative Kademlia; the direct recursive-vs-iterative comparison paper for the brief's explicit 'iterative versus recursive routing' subtopic, since the original Kademlia paper only argues for iterative routing without measuring against a recursive variant.

targets.title: SKIP+: A Self-Stabilizing Skip Graph
targets.authors: Riko Jacob, Andrea W. Richa, Christian Scheideler, Stefan Schmid, Hanjo Taubig
targets.why_needed: Proves a distributed algorithm that restores a valid skip graph from any weakly-connected state in polylogarithmic time without external intervention; the self-stabilization result the already-read HSkip+ paper's own self-stabilization proof is built directly on top of, needed to separate what HSkip+ itself proved from what it inherited from this paper.

targets.title: Survey on Algorithms for Self-Stabilizing Overlay Networks
targets.authors: Michael Feldmann, Christian Scheideler, Stefan Schmid
targets.why_needed: Found by forward-mining the already-read HSkip+ paper's citation list; the unified survey of the self-stabilizing-overlay literature (Skip+, HSkip+, and the lines that came after both), needed to check whether a design published after 2014 dominates HSkip+ on the same bandwidth-heterogeneity property before any selection is made.

targets.title: IPFS in the Fast Lane: Accelerating Record Storage with Optimistic Provide
targets.authors: Dennis Trautwein, Yiluo Wei, Yiannis Psaras, Moritz Schubotz, Ignacio Castro, Bela Gipp, Gareth Tyson
targets.why_needed: Measures Kademlia record-publish latency on the live IPFS DHT and states an optimistic-provide protocol change; a prior research pass in this project already cited specific latency percentiles (6.3s median, 20.6s p90, 49.8s p95) from this paper by title, and rule 1 requires those numbers re-extracted from the full text with their exact measurement conditions (node count, geographic distribution, DHT client version) before any later document may state them again.

targets.title: The Eternal Tussle: Exploring the Role of Centralization in IPFS
targets.authors: Yiluo Wei, Dennis Trautwein, Yiannis Psaras, Ignacio Castro, Will Scott, Aravindh Raman, Gareth Tyson
targets.why_needed: Measures how much of IPFS content-location traffic passes through a small number of centralized indexing and gateway services versus the Kademlia DHT itself; the 2024 update to the centralization-measurement literature the brief's already-summarized 2024 Wei et al. NSDI finding (one centralized indexer holding over 100x the DHT's location records) needs verified from full text before being restated with a number attached.

targets.title: The Cloud Strikes Back: Investigating the Decentralization of IPFS
targets.authors: Leonhard Balduf, Maciej Korczynski, Onur Ascigil, Navin V. Keizer, George Pavlou, Bjorn Scheuermann, Michal Krol
targets.why_needed: A second, independent 2023 measurement of IPFS centralization from a different author group than Wei et al. 2024; the brief requires presenting disagreeing measurements of the same system side by side with conditions stated, so both papers must be extracted even where their headline claims agree, to check whether their measurement methodologies and time windows actually agree too.

targets.title: Centralization in the Decentralized Web: Challenges and Opportunities in IPFS Data Management
targets.authors: Ruizhe Shi, Ruizhi Cheng, Yuqi Fu, Bo Han, Yue Cheng, Songqing Chen
targets.why_needed: A third, 2025 independent measurement of IPFS data replication and centralization (stated in search results as approximately 2.71% of files replicated more than 5 times); a third data point against Balduf 2023 and Wei 2024 needed to determine whether IPFS centralization is worsening, stable, or measured differently by each group before any trend claim is stated in the synthesis.

targets.title: Kadabra: Adapting Kademlia for the Decentralized Web
targets.authors: Yunqi Zhang, Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan
targets.why_needed: Proposes and states a measured lookup-latency and load-balance change to Kademlia specifically for content-addressed decentralized-web workloads (as opposed to the file-sharing workload Kademlia and KAD were designed and measured for); tests whether Kademlia's original design assumptions hold for a workload closer to the one this architecture targets.

targets.title: Scalability Limitations of Kademlia DHTs when Enabling Data Availability Sampling in Ethereum
targets.authors: Mikel Cortes-Goicoechea, Csaba Kiraly, Dmitriy Ryajov, Jose Luis Munoz-Tapia, Leonardo Bautista-Gomez
targets.why_needed: Measures Kademlia lookup latency and success rate under a specific high-query-rate workload (data availability sampling) at Ethereum-consensus-layer node counts; a stated case where a workload characteristic (query rate rather than churn) is the limiting factor on Kademlia performance, distinct from every churn-focused measurement already in this list.

notes:
Excluded from targets, per instructions, because already read in full by the prior pass: Kademlia (Maymounkov/Mazieres, IPTPS 2002), S/Kademlia (Baumgart/Mies, ICPADS 2007), HSkip+ (Feldotto/Scheideler/Graffi, P2P 2014). All three were forward-mined here (HSkip+ via Semantic Scholar's citations-by-DOI endpoint) rather than re-fetched; the two most relevant forward citations found are already targets above (FELDMANN-CSUR-21, and indirectly JACOB-JACM-14 as HSkip+'s own foundational dependency, found by reading HSkip+'s citation context in the prior-pass corpus text rather than by re-opening HSkip+ itself).

Citation-search yield versus fetch effort: DBLP was reachable and fast for every query in this pass. Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on approximately half of attempts even with 15-20 second delays between calls; the one successful call (HSkip+ citations by DOI) is the only Semantic Scholar bibliography-mining result in this pass. A later pass with more patience or a paced request schedule should re-run Semantic Scholar / OpenAlex forward-mining from Kademlia's own DOI directly (not attempted here — Kademlia's citation count is large enough that a full crawl needs its own budget), and from S/Kademlia's DOI, since only HSkip+ was mined this way.

On 'abandons the identifier-closeness premise entirely': no 2020s design found that abandons it outright. The two closest published examples are both from 2003-2004 (Kelips: replaces incremental identifier-closeness forwarding with gossip-maintained affinity groups and O(1) hops; Coral: keeps a DSHT but ranks routing choices by measured network proximity over identifier closeness and uses sloppy multi-valued hashing). DISC-NG (2024) was checked specifically for this and does NOT qualify — its advertisement-placement mechanism still runs over the existing Ethereum Kademlia DHT and still routes by identifier closeness; it changes advertisement density, not the routing metric. Flag this gap explicitly in synthesis rather than forcing a weak fit.

On Castro/Druschel/Hu/Rowstron 'Exploiting network proximity in peer-to-peer overlay networks' (the Microsoft Research technical report usually cited as the origin of proximity neighbor selection as a named technique, separate from the Pastry paper's brief mention of it): searched DBLP and Crossref under several title variants and found no indexed record — it appears to be an unpublished/tech-report-only document without a DOI. Per the verification rule (a citation must be checked against DBLP or Crossref, a guessed DOI is an error), it is NOT included as a target. The two indexed papers that carry the same content with a verifiable citation are already targets: ROWSTRON-MIDDLEWARE-01 (Pastry, which names PNS) and GUMMADI-SIGCOMM-03 (which analyzes PNS's effect across multiple routing geometries). If a later pass finds this tech report has since acquired a DOI or a stable institutional-repository record, add it.

BitTorrent Mainline DHT: found only pre-2020 measurement studies with confirmable citations (a 2016 DSC paper on Mainline DHT and Magnet Link measurement was the most recent DBLP-indexed hit) despite the brief's specific request for 2020-2026 deployed-DHT measurement. Web search for 2020s Mainline DHT measurement studies returned only citations to studies from 2010-2016. This is a gap: either no recent academic measurement of Mainline DHT exists, or it exists under search terms not tried yet (e.g., as a security/privacy paper rather than a 'measurement' paper — worth retrying with 'Mainline DHT' + 'attack' or + 'privacy' as the search phrase in a later pass). Not including the 2016 DSC paper as a target since it falls outside the 2020-2026 window this domain was asked to prioritize and its citation could not be fully confirmed (DBLP returned title/venue/year/DOI but the query did not resolve author names before time ran out); flagging rather than guessing.

All DOI fields either come directly from a DBLP hit's doi field or, where DBLP showed no DOI, from a matching Crossref record (HEEP-ATNAC-10, LI-INFOCOM-05); an empty string means neither source returned one, not that a DOI does not exist. Every candidate_url in this file returned HTTP 200 under curl -I / curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' at retrieval time, except: SHI-WWW-26 (arXiv 2601.16560 abstract page not independently curl-verified — venue/authors/DOI confirmed via DBLP only), CORTESGOICOECHEA-ARXIV-24 and ZHANG-FC-23 arXiv PDF links (verified reachable, but content was not opened past the abstract), and CASTRO-OSDI-02 / SINGH-INFOCOM-06 / GUMMADI-SIGCOMM-03 / STEINER-IMC-07 / STEINER-CCR-07 / JACOB-JACM-14(podc09 mirror) / HEEP-ATNAC-10 / FELDMANN-CSUR-21 / TRAUTWEIN-INFOCOM-24, all of which returned HTTP 200 and were spot-checked. FREEDMAN-NSDI-04, GUPTA-NSDI-04, MANKU-USITS-03, RHEA-USENIXATC-04, MALKHI-PODC-02, RATNASAMY-SIGCOMM-01, KAASHOEK-IPTPS-03, GUPTA-IPTPS-03 candidate URLs also returned HTTP 200. None of these 200 responses were read past the response header — a later pass must still verify each URL actually serves the claimed paper's full text and not a landing page, since a 200 status confirms reachability, not content match.
